title: Strictly semistable local uniformization along centred valuations
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $X$ be a $T$-curve with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There are finitely many integral strictly semistable $T$-curves $Y_i$ and birational quasi-modifications $Y_i\to X$ such that every centred valuation of every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$ lifts to some $Y_i$. Each generic map $(Y_i)_\eta\to X_\eta$ identifies $(Y_i)_\eta$ with an open subscheme. A $T$-curve means a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] $T$-scheme of pure relative dimension one, without a separatedness or properness assumption. Dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A $T$-curve is strictly semistable if, locally on it and on $T$, it admits an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] to $\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$ or $\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv-a))$, where $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an open of $T$ and $a\in A$; polynomial rings use [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. For an integral scheme $Y$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], its function field is the local ring at its generic point. A birational quasi-modification $Y\to Z$ is a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] identifying the function field of $Y$ with that of one irreducible component of the reduced scheme $Z$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. A centred valuation of that component means a valuation subring $W$ of its function field, together with a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}W\to Z$ inducing the generic-point map. It lifts to $Y$ when this morphism factors through $Y$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, pp. 29--30; applied componentwise when the smooth generic fibre is disconnected; primary PDF read online, local archival copy WANTED (see report.md).
